nodes.label: Highblossom Design System
Creative North Star: Precision Fitting as a Digital Interface
nodes.rationale: The design system reflects the precision, durability and high-end nature of fitted glass, balancing industrial brutalist utility with a premium dark aesthetic.

nodes.label: The Contrast Rule
nodes.rationale: Avoid middle-gray values: every surface is either a deep black or a high-contrast white/accent, which is what keeps the premium feel.

nodes.label: The State Rule
nodes.rationale: Every interactive element must have a visible transition to the accent colour on hover or focus.

nodes.label: Glass Cards component treatment
nodes.rationale: Premium containers mimic the physical glass product: admin surface fill with backdrop blur, 1px subtle border, surface-alt on hover.

nodes.label: Design language v1 — the `ui` token layer
nodes.rationale: Introduced with the auth redesign as the reusable base for migrating public pages one at a time. Deliberately additive and opt-in: it lives beside the frozen legacy systems so no unmigrated page changes, which makes a half-migrated app a normal, safe state.
nodes.source_location: # Design language v1 — the `ui` token layer

nodes.label: Frozen legacy token namespaces (Flux/Material-3, admin, site, booking)
nodes.rationale: One CSS bundle (app.css) is shared by every surface, so repointing --color-site-*, --color-admin-*, --booking-* or --color-primary restints site, admin and auth in a single edit. Those namespaces are therefore frozen and app.css is off-limits as a styling lever.

nodes.label: .hb-ui body scope via x-layouts::base
nodes.rationale: Rendering through x-layouts::base puts .hb-ui on the body and opts the page into v1; the v1 CSS is unlayered but scoped to that class so it can beat app.css without touching anything else.

nodes.label: Unlayered CSS beats @layer utilities; .ui-field/.ui-btn are authoritative
nodes.rationale: app.css component classes are unlayered, so focus:ring-* utilities lose to the global *:focus-visible rule; utility classes added to an element carrying .ui-field or .ui-btn will not win — change the CSS once or use the component prop. Alpine :bindings must go on plain elements because on a Blade component tag they compile as PHP.
nodes.source_location: ### Specificity rules that are not obvious

nodes.label: Photographic hero surface: the one scoped --hero-* exception
nodes.rationale: The cinematic homepage hero paints type over unknown photography, so it is allowed exactly four deviations, only inside .hb-hero and only through page-scoped --hero-* properties (never in app.css, never touching --*-ui-*). Gradient-fill display type is legal there because it is a photographic treatment of one decorative word, not a heading style; contrast is carried by --hero-scrim rather than by the ink.

nodes.label: x-ui.* component library (button, input, field, card, link, alert-banner, ...)
nodes.rationale: Components live in resources/views/components/ui/. x-ui.input derives aria-invalid, aria-describedby and old() from the validation key; x-ui.field owns error presentation so a red border is never hand-written; x-ui.link adds rel="noopener noreferrer" for external targets, which the legacy markup omitted.

nodes.label: DOM contracts owned by js/tests, not styling
nodes.rationale: Passkey hooks, submit-pending attributes, password-toggle data-*, Fortify field names, novalidate on all auth forms and the single x-dialog/adminConfirm overlay contract are behavioural seams: restyle freely, do not rename or remove them.

nodes.label: Validation is server-side and the app owns the sentences
nodes.rationale: The original 'do not change validation rules' brief is superseded for auth forms by a user instruction; auth logic, routes, middleware and throttling stay untouched. novalidate stops the browser pre-empting the server, rules moved to first-party request classes with messages()/attributes() so an error names the box the user sees, global lang/en/validation.php is left alone because copy is per-form, and bail keeps one message per field. remember gets no rule (a checkbox only sends on/1/nothing and boolean would reject 'on'); two-factor code keeps Fortify's nullable|string because Alpine auto-submits at six digits.

nodes.label: Banner vs field error split (App\Support\AuthNotification)
nodes.rationale: A page-level sentence (failed credentials, lockout, invalid token) owns the banner and everything else stays under its own input via aria-describedby. Promoting one field's sentence into the banner left that box red with nothing written under it — the opposite of what the split is for — so a bag of only field errors now reads 'Please check the highlighted fields.' Login enumeration stays symmetric; the forgot-password copy is not, and changing it is a product decision, so it is flagged not fixed.

nodes.label: Rate limiting is a status page, not a banner
nodes.rationale: Fortify's throttle throws 429, so the sixth attempt renders errors/429.blade.php; surfacing seconds-remaining inside the login view would require changing exception handling, which is out of scope for a visual pass.
nodes.source_location: ## Rate limiting is a status page

nodes.label: Brand colour / headline font debt: Cabinet Grotesk never loaded
nodes.rationale: Google Fonts does not host Cabinet Grotesk (the request 400s), so every display heading has silently fallen back to the generic sans stack. v1 drops the display face and carries hierarchy on weight; fixing --font-headline globally would change site and admin headings in one edit, so it is deferred to rollout step 2.

nodes.label: Brand colour debt: declared oxblood #73081d vs rendered red #dc2626
nodes.rationale: v1 uses the red the site, admin and booking flow already render rather than the declared oxblood --color-primary, because repointing the declared value would restint every existing surface; the mismatch is written down as debt rather than silently resolved.

nodes.label: v1 rollout plan: swap the layout, then the components, never globally
nodes.rationale: Five page groups ordered by risk, auth first and the homepage (ContentBlocks, parallax, SEO) last. Deferred decisions that step 2 must settle: --font-headline, the oxblood-vs-red debt, and whether admin adopts v1 at all.

nodes.label: The day desk — admin dashboard and System Overview
nodes.rationale: Built to the Awwwards craft bar but scaled to an operations surface for a glass shop: no loader, no WebGL, no cursor follower. The job is to say what today is, where in it you are and what is late in under three seconds. Concept A (the day rail) won over 'plate and pane' and 'the glazing schedule' because its anchor is real code — the app already computes slot spans and bay capacity.

nodes.label: The Day Rail signature: every job is a span whose length is its duration
nodes.rationale: Today is drawn as a measuring rail with a now line on the real clock, so the page is a glazier's setting-out drawing rather than a row of stat cards. Phone recomposes it into a vertical timeline because the ordering and durations are the information, not the horizontal position.

nodes.label: --dash-* token layer scoped to .hb-dash / .hb-desk / .hb-sheet
nodes.rationale: No global token is repointed: the admin surfaces read their own --dash-* values declared in admin(-desk).css and re-declared inside html.dark, so a theme switch flips the whole surface from one place. Dark values are lifted to clear AA where the light value would not. The scoring bench deliberately narrows the accent to a single claim: a value that is not what is stored.

nodes.label: Geist Mono is reserved for measured values
nodes.rationale: Times, durations, counts, deltas, references, plates and setting keys are mono with tabular-nums; --font-mono is not repointed in @theme because that would restint Flux and every other admin page, so a scoped .hb-dash-mono class is used instead. This makes the legacy 'use Geist Mono for numerical data' rule true for the first time.

nodes.label: One clock, no new dependencies (single requestAnimationFrame module)
nodes.rationale: GSAP, Lenis and OGL are not installed and not added: the repo and deploy stay lean, and the shell owns its scroll so Lenis would be wrong anyway. One rAF loop in admin.js drives the now line, the clock and the day state, stops when closed or hidden, unmounts on livewire:navigated, and never starts under prefers-reduced-motion. Idle motion is real or it is nothing — the overview stays still because animating a snapshot probe would be a lie.

nodes.label: Reduced motion stops movement and keeps state
nodes.rationale: The reduced-motion block kills the draw, the wipe, the foot's slide and the arrow's travel and leaves every mark, count and sentence exactly where it was: state is carried by colour and text, never by movement. The block lives once in the CSS layer, never per component.

nodes.label: The scoring bench — Company Settings and Profile
nodes.rationale: Two of the largest forms in the app (115 inputs behind one PUT). The design targets the real failure mode — where is the thing, what else did I touch, did that save — rather than decoration. No new colours and no repointed token: it inherits the day desk's --dash-* values, since consistency across the same shop, same people, same screen is a Design win.

nodes.label: The score line: a red rule on every row that diverges from stored
nodes.rationale: A value genuinely sits in two states at once — the row in company_settings and the characters in the box — so the mark is that delta and it is computable in the browser. The concept only exists because one commit stands behind a hundred and fifteen inputs. Plan correction: marks are not 'wiped one group at a time' on commit, because a commit is a POST and a redirect; what retracts is a mark the person undoes.

nodes.label: resources/js/admin-sheet.js marks engine
nodes.rationale: Delegated input/change/click listeners recompute marks in one pass; requestAnimationFrame is used only as a cancelled coalescer. Baseline is taken from the DOM (because an empty repeater has no rows yet), rows already carrying a validation error are excluded from the baseline so a refused save reads as uncommitted, and state is rebuilt per page rather than kept in a module singleton because the admin shell is a @persist island.

nodes.label: The measured row: 20px gutter | 13rem meta | 1fr control
nodes.rationale: One straightedge for the whole sheet is what makes 115 fields readable — no card per field and no label stacked above its input. Per-section layout variety is explicitly rejected on a form: different label placement per group is the fastest way to make the sheet unreadable. Variance is placed where it carries meaning (plates, repeater stacks, sample tiles, state cards, env rows).

nodes.label: No scroll reveals on a form
nodes.rationale: A form whose fields arrive as you scroll is a form you cannot tab through predictably; the desk's data-dash-reveal exists because a dashboard is read in bands. Every field is present and painted at once, and the exception is written down rather than quietly skipped.

nodes.label: Pinned names, attribute order and visible strings asserted by tests
nodes.rationale: Around 90 input names, two attribute-order regexes, x-ref literals, tab keys and a long list of visible strings are asserted by 13 test files, so two controls stay hand-written raw markup and are never converted to a component. A restyle must keep every wire:* hook and Livewire attribute.

nodes.label: The button emphasis ladder (primary / secondary / danger / commit)
nodes.rationale: Rounds six to nine converged on: a destructive control says so with a genuine 2px ink edge, red inside an ask stays red and deepens on hover, and the primary keeps its face and deepens rather than demoting itself to a ghost. The cause of the worst regressions was ownership, not intent — three passes each added button rules in their own section, so file order rather than any decision picked the winner, and a restatement four :not() deep silently killed every plain button's hover. All four roles now live in one ordered block at the end of admin-sheet.css.
nodes.source_location: ## Round eight, and the bug the fixes caused

nodes.label: Red on the sheet has exactly one meaning: a value that is not what is stored
nodes.rationale: Because the mark owns red, focus is ink rather than the shell's red halo (a red ring on every tab stop would have made one claim mean two things), the x-ui.checkbox tick is re-inked inside .hb-sheet only without touching the component's 43 other usages, and inside an ask — where there are no values and no marks — red is free again and belongs on the answer that destroys.

nodes.label: Known and not fixed: throttled mobile LCP is the shared admin bundle
nodes.rationale: The admin loads app.css (60.6 kB gzipped carrying every Tailwind utility the public site uses), admin.css, the Livewire/Alpine runtime and admin.js, which puts throttled mobile LCP at 10-13s while unthrottled the same pages measure 1.0-1.3s. Splitting the admin bundle is a shell change touching every public page's CSS delivery and the Vite entry graph, so it is named and offered rather than shipped.

nodes.label: Env rows on the sheet: locked by default, allowlist only
nodes.rationale: Only the admin-editable allowlist appears on the sheet and the sheet says so; stored values reach the marks engine through data-* written by json_encode() and never for the env rows, because @json inside an attribute is unsafe with this local PHP (it ignores JSON_HEX_QUOT).

nodes.label: admin.css is unlayered, so display there outranks hidden and every sm: utility
nodes.rationale: The scoped admin layers therefore set only position, width, clip-path, border and background, declare display inside the media query that needs it, and put [hidden] back in its rights.

nodes.label: Content after </x-layouts::admin> is never emitted
nodes.rationale: Every @push must precede the component close; the same boundary reappears in the rollout plan for detail pages.
